title: Why Do Some Nuclei Grow? The Critical Radius

speech_units.raw_text: Why do some tiny nuclei dissolve while others grow? Energy competition decides.
speech_units.display_text: Why do some tiny nuclei dissolve while others grow? Energy competition decides.
speech_units.spoken_text: Why do some tiny nuclei dissolve while others grow? Energy competition decides.

speech_units.raw_text: Classical homogeneous nucleation models a spherical nucleus with two terms: a positive surface cost and a negative bulk gain.
speech_units.display_text: Classical homogeneous nucleation models a spherical nucleus with two terms: a positive surface cost and a negative bulk gain.
speech_units.spoken_text: Classical homogeneous nucleation models a spherical nucleus with two terms: a positive surface cost and a negative bulk gain.

speech_units.raw_text: Surface cost scales as radius squared; bulk gain scales as radius cubed.
speech_units.display_text: Surface cost scales as radius squared; bulk gain scales as radius cubed.
speech_units.spoken_text: Surface cost scales as radius squared; bulk gain scales as radius cubed.

speech_units.raw_text: At small radii, surface cost dominates and free energy rises. As the nucleus grows, bulk gain takes over.
speech_units.display_text: At small radii, surface cost dominates and free energy rises. As the nucleus grows, bulk gain takes over.
speech_units.spoken_text: At small radii, surface cost dominates and free energy rises. As the nucleus grows, bulk gain takes over.

speech_units.raw_text: The curve peaks at the critical radius. Below it, shrinking is favored; above it, growth lowers free energy.
speech_units.display_text: The curve peaks at the critical radius. Below it, shrinking is favored; above it, growth lowers free energy.
speech_units.spoken_text: The curve peaks at the critical radius. Below it, shrinking is favored; above it, growth lowers free energy.

speech_units.raw_text: The critical radius equals two gamma divided by the bulk driving-force magnitude.
speech_units.display_text: The critical radius equals two gamma divided by the bulk driving-force magnitude.
speech_units.spoken_text: The critical radius equals two gamma divided by the bulk driving-force magnitude.

speech_units.raw_text: The barrier scales as interfacial energy cubed divided by driving force squared.
speech_units.display_text: The barrier scales as interfacial energy cubed divided by driving force squared.
speech_units.spoken_text: The barrier scales as interfacial energy cubed divided by driving force squared.

speech_units.raw_text: Assumptions: a spherical nucleus, homogeneous nucleation, an isotropic interface. Real systems also depend on interface structure, anisotropy, and kinetics.
speech_units.display_text: Assumptions: a spherical nucleus, homogeneous nucleation, an isotropic interface. Real systems also depend on interface structure, anisotropy, and kinetics.
speech_units.spoken_text: Assumptions: a spherical nucleus, homogeneous nucleation, an isotropic interface. Real systems also depend on interface structure, anisotropy, and kinetics.
